To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the runtime distribution of backtrack procedures for SAT and CSP are often characterized by heavy tails, and that random restarts can significantly improve performance by eliminating heavy tails and exploiting short runs.

(1) runtime distributions for SAT and CSP are often best described by heavy-tailed distributions; (2) the left-hand tail of these distributions indicates that a small fraction of short runs is sufficient to obtain a good approximation to the expected runtime; (3) random restarts eliminate heavy-tailedness and take advantage of the small fraction of short, successful runs; (4) the resulting speedups can be substantial.
